chunks: Sahl raised it (in the chain) and said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so that he would look at his nakedness'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father entering the bathhouse with his son in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a specific legal ruling for the bathhouse context, prohibiting a father from entering with his son to prevent the casual observation of the son's awrah. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving modesty (haya) even within close familial bonds, ensuring that private parts remain covered to maintain spiritual and physical dignity during daily hygiene practices.

en.hubeali: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so that he would look at his nakedness’.
en.sarwar: A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ’Isma‘il ibn Yasar from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan al-Sadusiy from Bashir al-Nabbal who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about using a bathhouse. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you want to take a bath?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I like to take a bath.’ He (the Imam) commanded to warm up the bathhouse. He then entered in it and wore a loincloth, which covered from his belly button down to his knees. Then he commanded the owner of the bathhouse to apply on him (lime or oil) on what was not covered by the loincloth. Then he (the Imam) asked him to move away. He (the Imam) then applied with his hand on the area under the loincloth and said, ‘This is how you must take a bath.’”
